options.text: Vaccination helps the immune system build protection so later contact with the same pathogen is less likely to cause serious illness.
Vaccines are medicines taken only after someone is already sick, to cure that illness.
Children living on the same street always have the same immunity and fall ill equally often.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Rohan's class discusses how immunity and vaccination protect people from serious infections such as measles and tetanus.

part_answers.answer: Vaccines prepare the immune system beforehand; people in similar surroundings can still differ in how well they fight disease.

teacher.key_rationale: Immunity is the body's ability to fight disease; vaccines help the immune system develop protection against serious infections before or around exposure. Vaccines are not only post-illness cures, and shared surroundings do not force equal immunity.
